scenario_premise: One synthetic display card receives notice revisions and deliveries in a deliberately different order. This checks ledger ordering behavior only; it does not establish event truth or real clock behavior.

ordering_contract_assumption.notice_version: A synthetic, card-scoped logical version. Higher versions supersede lower versions for current notice state.
ordering_contract_assumption.event_occurred_at: A synthetic source occurrence time. Preserve it as evidence, but do not use it to infer receive order or real clock skew.
ordering_contract_assumption.received_at: Synthetic ledger arrival/processing time, separate from occurrence time and notice version.
ordering_contract_assumption.same_version_same_semantics: A second delivery with the same notice version and equivalent semantic content, even under a different transport intent ID, is a duplicate and must not add a card revision or notification action.
ordering_contract_assumption.lower_version_after_higher: A lower version arriving after a higher accepted version is stale. Record the ignored attempt for audit, but do not change current card state or emit another notification.
ordering_contract_assumption.scope_warning: This is a local test contract, not an approved production rule or a claim that private V2 specifies version semantics this way.

source_independence: NOT_ASSERTED; all messages use one synthetic source label.

arrival_order_only_negative_control_expe.interpretation: The unversioned arrival-order ledger accepts every fresh intent ID as new. A late lower-version correction regresses the card, a duplicate cancellation emits another action, and an old active message arriving after cancellation restores ACTIVE. This is a negative control, not desired behavior.

unsupported_items: Actual wall-clock skew or source clock correctness.
Production rules for assigning, skipping, or conflicting notice versions.
Same-version messages with conflicting semantic content.
Reopening a cancelled notice with a later version.
Transport receipt identity and retry guarantees in a real delivery system.
Real notification emission, user visibility, acknowledgment, or efficacy.
Physical-event truth, alert correctness, and source independence.
